stories.headline: Russian Drone Strike Hits Kryvyi Rih Mall in Double-Tap Attack
stories.body:
A Russian double-tap drone strike targeted the largest shopping center in Kryvyi Rih, leaving many dead and injured [c1, c2]. News outlets and regional officials gave varying casualty numbers following the attack [c1, c6, c7]. The BBC reported that at least 15 people were killed in the strike [c1]. In contrast, Al Jazeera reported that 14 people were killed [c6]. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Ganzha also stated that the drone strikes on the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre killed 14 people [c7].

The number of reported injuries from the mall attack also varied across reports [c2, c6, c7]. The BBC stated that 130 people were injured, including 23 children, when the drone attack struck Kryvyi Rih's largest mall [c2]. Al Jazeera reported that the strike injured over 100 people, including 22 children [c6]. Meanwhile, Oleksandr Ganzha stated that the drone strikes wounded 121 others [c7]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the second wave of the drone strike specifically targeted emergency workers who were responding to the scene [c3].

Russian strikes were reported in other areas of Ukraine as well [c4, c11]. Separate Russian attacks in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region killed four people, including three children [c4]. In the Kharkiv region, a separate Russian drone strike killed two women, aged 73 and 66, and injured two other people [c11].

Ukrainian forces also conducted drone strikes across the border inside Russia [c9, c10, c12]. A Ukrainian drone attack struck a car near Razumnoye in Russia's Belgorod region, killing one person and wounding four others [c9]. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that a Ukrainian drone attack hit an oil refinery in Perm as well as the Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd [c10]. Russia's Defence Ministry stated that its air defences intercepted 325 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions and Crimea [c12].

The drone strikes occur as the broader conflict continues [c5]. Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 [c5]. Moscow currently controls about a fifth of Ukrainian territory [c5]. Meanwhile, international political leaders are preparing for diplomatic discussions regarding Ukraine [c8]. The Coalition of the Willing meeting, set to take place on Ukraine's independence day, will be co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham [c8].

vocab.meaning: stopped or caught something before it reached its destination
an industrial factory where raw materials like oil are processed

stories.headline: Turkey Requests Interpol Arrest Warrants for Israeli Leaders Over Flotilla Raid
stories.body:
Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey has requested Interpol red notices for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and another suspect [c13]. The request relates to an attack in May on the Global Sumud Flotilla [c13]. Earlier, on July 14, Turkey issued arrest warrants against 35 people on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, and torture related to the Gaza aid flotilla interception [c14]. Among those named in Turkish arrest warrants is Israeli soldier Afek Moskovitch, who faces charges including genocide and torture [c16]. France, Italy, and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings regarding Israel's detention of activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla [c17].

In response to the legal actions, Benjamin Netanyahu's office called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an antisemitic dictator who massacred Kurds and supports Hamas [c15, c18]. Netanyahu's office added that Erdogan's attempt to intimidate Israeli leaders will go nowhere [c15]. In a separate regional development, Syria accused Israel of striking a disused military air base located near Aleppo [c19].

vocab.meaning: official legal documents issued by a court authorizing arrests
frighten or threaten someone to make them do what one wants

stories.headline: Hong Kong Court Convicts Former Tiananmen Vigil Leaders Under Security Law
stories.body:
A panel of three judges in Hong Kong has convicted former Tiananmen vigil organizers Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung for incitement to subversion [c20]. Lee Cheuk-yan, aged 69, and Chow Hang-tung, aged 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison under Hong Kong's national security law [c21]. Former Hong Kong lawmaker Albert Ho, who was a co-defendant in the subversion trial, pleaded guilty in January [c22].

The subversion case against their organization, the Hong Kong Alliance, focused on its slogan demanding an end to one-party rule [c24]. The Hong Kong Alliance was originally founded in May 1989 to support student pro-democracy rallies in Beijing [c25]. Chow Hang-tung previously had her 2022 conviction overturned by Hong Kong's top court regarding a 2021 arrest for inciting the public to join the Tiananmen vigil [c26]. While in detention, Chow Hang-tung wrote a letter from prison to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, urging Britain to adopt a more robust stance against China [c23].

vocab.meaning: an attempt to weaken or overturn a government or political system
strong, forceful, and firm in position

stories.headline: Jailed Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan Sent for Hospital Check-Up
stories.body:
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly taken to an Islamabad hospital for a court-ordered medical examination before being returned to Adiala Jail hours later [c27]. Khan was originally arrested in 2023, sentenced to three years in prison on corruption charges, and disqualified from politics for five years [c34]. In January 2025, Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi were sentenced to 14 years and seven years in prison, respectively, in a separate corruption case [c30].

Relatives of Imran Khan stated that he is being subjected to torture in prison [c28]. His son Kasim stated in February that Khan had lost most of the vision in his right eye, leaving him with only 15 percent eyesight [c29]. Following the latest examination, Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that a team of qualified doctors declared Khan medically fit [c31].

Security concerns altered the medical visit [c32]. Imran Khan was transferred to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences instead of the court-ordered private Shifa International Hospital [c32]. A senior police official told the BBC that a heavy police presence placed outside Shifa International Hospital was used as a decoy [c33].

vocab.meaning: something used to distract or trick people away from the main target
officially declared ineligible or unfit to participate

stories.headline: UK, Australia, and Canada Condemn Israel Over Halted World Central Kitchen Probe
stories.body:
The UK, Australia, and Canada issued a joint statement calling Israel's decision not to conduct a criminal investigation into an April 2024 strike on a World Central Kitchen convoy shameful [c35]. The Israeli drone strike in April 2024 killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers, including three Britons, an Australian, a Pole, a dual US-Canadian national, and a Palestinian [c36]. Following the Israeli military's announcement that it would not pursue criminal investigations into the attack, Poland and Australia summoned Israel's ambassadors [c37]. The joint statement noted that 186 humanitarian workers were killed in Gaza in 2025 [c38]. One of the Israeli military officers dismissed over the convoy strike had previously signed an open letter calling for Gaza to be deprived of humanitarian aid [c42].

In other military announcements, the Israeli military stated it will conduct a criminal investigation into the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab and six relatives, as well as the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinians [c39]. Meanwhile, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called Israel's tender for 1,200 settlement homes in the West Bank's E1 area an unacceptable and destructive act [c40]. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar rejected Miliband's statement, asserting that Jewish people have the right to live throughout the Land of Israel [c41].

vocab.meaning: a group of vehicles traveling together for protection or aid
officially called someone to appear or attend a meeting

stories.headline: US and Canada Negotiate Trade Deal as Trump Tariff Deadline Looms
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has threatened to impose a 50 percent tariff on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods starting Saturday at 12:01am EDT [c43]. In response, Canadian Minister Dominic LeBlanc met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in Washington, DC, for over three hours to negotiate a trade deal [c44]. Political pressure is building inside Canada [c45, c46, c47]. A Leger Opinion poll showed that 56 percent of Canadians do not want Prime Minister Mark Carney to make further trade concessions to the US [c45]. Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew called Donald Trump very weak and urged Canada to fight rather than make concessions [c47]. In a leaked audio recording, US Vice President JD Vance mocked Prime Minister Carney for attempting to out-tough Trump [c46].

Tensions over trade have already affected alcohol sales [c48, c49]. The White House stated that Canadian imports of US alcohol dropped approximately 81 percent year-on-year following Canadian retaliatory measures [c48]. Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston and Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew confirmed that Prime Minister Carney asked Canadian provinces to allow US alcohol back on store shelves [c49].

vocab.meaning: things that are granted or yielded in response to demands
done in return to harm someone who has harmed you first

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi Stages Sit-In Protest Over Student Pellet Gun Injury in Delhi
stories.body:
Indian political leader Rahul Gandhi staged a seven-hour sit-in protest outside the office of New Delhi's Deputy Commissioner of Police to demand formal police action regarding an injured student [c50]. Gandhi's protest demanded a First Information Report, known as an FIR, over severe pellet gun injuries suffered by 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab [c50]. During a student march in Delhi on July 20, Sahil Lochab sustained over 200 pellets in his body and lost vision in his right eye [c51]. Following Rahul Gandhi's sit-in protest, Delhi Police registered an FIR under Sections 118(1) and 125 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [c52]. Rahul Gandhi claimed that the final approval to register the FIR came directly from Home Secretary and Union Home Minister Amit Shah [c57].

The police actions taken during the July 20 student protest have drawn conflicting reports and claims from government figures and security forces [c54, c58]. A general diary entry recorded at the Sansad Marg police station stated that Rapid Action Force personnel fired two rounds from anti-riot guns [c54]. However, an inquiry conducted by the Central Reserve Police Force found that Rapid Action Force personnel actually fired seven pellet rounds [c54]. In contrast to reports of severe injuries, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju claimed that no protester was seriously injured or suffered broken bones during the July 20 police action [c58].

Official investigations and political fallout followed the demonstration [c53, c55, c56]. The Supreme Court of India constituted a five-member High-Powered Enquiry Committee, headed by a former Supreme Court judge, to investigate the police action during the July 20 protest [c53]. The political impact was also felt in the national cabinet, where Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following opposition protests over police action against student demonstrators [c55].

Government figures attacked Rahul Gandhi's motivations for staging the demonstration [c56]. Union Minister JP Nadda criticized Rahul Gandhi's sit-in as camera-centric drama designed to distract from criticism regarding the national song and flag [c56].

vocab.meaning: officially formed, established, or set up
the adverse results or consequences of a situation

stories.headline: Indian Government Rules Out Ethanol Diversion as Sugar Prices Increase
stories.body:
The Indian government estimated domestic sugar production for the current season at 306 lakh tonnes, which is 11 percent lower than the initial estimate of 343 lakh tonnes [c59]. Lower supply contributed to rising costs, with retail sugar prices in India reaching Rs 58.2 per kg, representing a 20 percent increase over the previous month [c61]. Regional differences emerged across the country [c63]. Odisha registered the highest retail sugar price in India at Rs 64.72 per kg, which is up Rs 17.80 compared to the same date in 2025 [c63]. International sugar prices also rose, jumping more than 16 percent to $552 per tonne on August 20 from $474 per tonne on June 30 [c65].

The government rejected claims that sugar shortages were caused by ethanol production [c62]. Official data showed the share of Indian sugar diverted for ethanol production declined from around 12 percent in 2022-23 to around 9 percent in 2025-26 [c62]. To address the shortage and stabilize domestic prices, the Indian government permitted the duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar [c60]. It also imposed a stock limit of 400 tonnes on sugar dealers from August 1 to November 30 [c64]. Meanwhile, payment processing remained high, as 97 percent of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 season had been paid to Indian farmers as of August 20 [c66].

vocab.meaning: turned aside from its main course or intended purpose
make something steady and unlikely to change or fail

stories.headline: Twenty-Two Indian Sailors Safe After Ships Hijacked Off Yemen and Somalia
stories.body:
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that 22 Indian seafarers aboard two hijacked merchant vessels off Yemen and Somalia are safe [c67]. The first incident involved the Eritrea-flagged oil products tanker MT Sibu 1 [c68]. The vessel, carrying 16 Indians among its 20 crew members, was hijacked by six armed pirates off the coast of Yemen on August 20 [c68].

The second incident involved the Cameroon-flagged cargo ship MV Lutuf, which was hijacked off Somalia's Puntland coast on August 17 [c69]. The ship was carrying six Indians among its 10 crew members [c69]. During the attack, eight armed pirates carrying AK-47-type weapons boarded the MV Lutuf from two skiffs and forced the crew from the citadel to the bridge [c71]. The MV Lutuf was carrying Turkish weapons, communications, and satellite equipment bound for a Turkish military training facility located in Mogadishu [c70]. India plays a key role in global maritime shipping, as the 2026 BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report estimates India supplies 311,936 seafarers, making it the second-largest supplier globally [c72].

vocab.meaning: connected with the sea, seafaring, or nautical commerce
people who work or travel on ships at sea

stories.headline: Supreme Court Cuts Legal Practice Requirement for Entry-Level Indian Judges
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India ruled in a 2-1 majority that advocates with one year of practice are eligible to apply for entry-level judicial officer posts, reducing the prior three-year requirement [c73]. Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice A G Masih formed the majority opinion, while Justice Vinod Chandran dissented [c74].

Under the new rules, candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment between May 25, 2025, and March 31, 2027, will be deemed to meet the one-year legal practice requirement without needing to provide proof certificates [c76]. However, starting April 1, 2027, candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment must produce a certificate of proof of practice showing participation in effective judicial proceedings [c77].

Once selected, judicial candidates will undergo a mandatory two-year post-selection training period [c75]. During their first year of training, candidates will receive fixed emoluments equal to half the salary of magistrates [c75]. The comprehensive post-selection judicial training program includes one year at a State judicial academy, six months of clerkship under a Principal District Judge, and six months under a High Court judge [c78].

vocab.meaning: disagreed with the official or majority opinion
salaries, fees, or profits earned from employment or office
